title: metadata-protocol: publish-drafts build probes query datasets with no execution context, so a correct dataset widget is reported as an error-tier widget_query_failed
body:
Filing gate: ① a product defect with a named location and a live reproduction (finding class (a)).
Reader: the `packages/metadata-protocol` lane (`build-probes.ts`, the dataset probe call), next PR touching publish-time probes.
Dedupe (open AND closed): "publish-drafts build probes widget_query_failed access denied dataset no execution context" → 6 hits, none on this (nearest: #10377, same-batch dataset closure; #8400/#8594/#8595, publish audit rows — all different defects).
reach: public HTTP entry, measured twice — `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/publish-drafts` answers an error-tier `widget_query_failed` for a widget that renders correctly.
Checklist item priority: P1
type: Bug
QA-source: #25479 · studio-authoring.draft-publish-lifecycle · observed beside the clauses

## What happens

After `POST /api/v1/packages/PKG/publish-drafts` publishes a dashboard whose widget is bound to a valid dataset (`showcase_task_metrics`), the response's `data.probes.issues` carries an **error-severity** `widget_query_failed`: `[Analytics] Access denied: reading "showcase_task" is not permitted for this user`, with fix text "Fix the dataset definition…". The same widget renders correctly for the admin who published it and for the member Mei. So the probe reports a defect that does not exist and tells the author to fix a correct dataset. The per-item publish runs no probes, which is why this appears only on the package publish.

Reproduced twice (two dashboards in one batch, then a third alone) on `main` 77392e90.

## Mechanism

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts` (around line 343) calls the analytics service with no execution context:

```
const result = await analytics.queryDataset(dataset, selection, undefined);
```

Read admission refuses a context-less read, so every dataset over a permission-gated object fails the probe. The probe's own docblock says it runs "the SAME `queryDataset` path the dashboard renderer hits", and the renderer passes the caller's context.

**Expected:** the probe runs in the publishing caller's context, or in an explicit system context for a build check. Either way a correct dataset produces no error-tier issue.
